note: PASS WITH CAVEATS. (1) ITEM_17 IS NOT AN ITEM RESPONSE -- shipped with blank item_text and blank option_text. In the S1 File workbook (PLOS ONE 10.1371/journal.pone.0197276.s001, sheet Hoja1) the column headed 'Item 17' (0-based col 25, the first of the 'Increasing challenging Job Demands' block) does not hold 1-5 responses: 141 of its 202 values are non-integers taking exact quarters (1.5, 2.25, 2.5, 2.75, ...), and it equals the mean of the four columns 'Item 18'..'Item 21' in 200 of 202 rows. The workbook's own challenging-block Subtotal (col 30, =AVERAGE(Z:AD)) is algebraically identical to it. data/dominguez_2018_job_crafting.py melts that column as item_17 and applies astype(int), so the live table's item_17 is floor() of a 4-item composite: live counts 1/46/103/46/6 reproduce trunc() of the column exactly. Attaching the canonical DJCS item 17 wording ('When an interesting project comes along, I offer myself proactively as project co-worker') would have been false, so no text is shipped for it. This is a defect in the RESPONSE table, not in the extraction, and it is worth an IRW data-fix issue: item_17 should probably be dropped from dominguez_2018_jcs. (2) LANGUAGE FALLBACK: the study administered a Spanish version of the DJCS in Colombia (paper's ref 44, Ficapal-Cusi et al. 2014 IN3 working paper). No Spanish wording exists in the deposit (the S1 workbook carries only 'Item 1'..'Item 21' headers, the four subscale names and the English anchor legend) or in the paper's body, which quotes four items in English only. English canonical wording is therefore shipped in the base fields with text_source=translated_substitute, language=Spanish and empty _translated columns, per the itemtext standard's fallback. (3) MAPPING is PARTIAL: item_N = workbook column N is proven cell-for-cell, and the four subscale blocks reproduce the paper's published skill means (4.505/2.719/3.862 vs 4.50/2.71/3.86); nothing in the data separates items within a block. (4) wording_rights=NC set on every row: arnoldbakker.com/questionnaires-details (retrieved 2026-09-04) states 'These questionnaires can be used for free in scientific research. Those who want to use the questionnaires commercially, need to contact Dr. Bakker.' The list of covered questionnaires is behind a login, so that the JCS is on it could not be confirmed directly; the flag is set conservatively. The table still ships because IRW's copy of the wording is from a CC BY 4.0 source (Nursing Reports 14(4), PMC11587447, Table 2), not from Bakker's own restricted download -- the source-licence rule of itemtext_standard.md (ECR-R ruling, 2026-09-04). The sibling dominguez_2018_uwes is blocked because for the UWES the rights holders' NC-clause manual IS the only source of the administered wording.
